answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with cross-issuer credential binding. Each identity is anchored to two independent credentials: a hardware attestation, plus an endorsement from an agent in the participant atlas. Both are soulbound to one on-chain identity, a kernel that cannot be copied or sold. A registry hashes each credential; one appearing under two identities flags both. Like light through a prism, one real backing yields only one valid identity, so attackers must buy fresh hardware and trust per fake agent while honest agents pay once.
